newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania president offers ousted predecessor a home.
newsitem.headline: Romania president offers ousted predecessor a home.

text.p: President Emil Constantinescu called on Friday for laws to enable his ex-communist predecessor to keep the home and bodyguards he had while in office.

But Ion Iliescu, who led Romania for seven years after the execution of dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, declined the offer. He says he bought the apartment legally like hundreds of thousands of sitting tenants in the post-communist era.

"The president has asked the government to draft a law that will grant former president Ion Iliescu and his wife a house free of charge for the rest of their lives," a statement from Constantinescu's office said.
Constantinescu said the gesture was motivated by a legal void on the status of former leaders in the Balkan state.
But Iliescu, quoted by Bucharest dailies, said: "I don't need an official house as a former head of state. I didn't even have one when I was president."
Iliescu has been accused by the new centrist government of using his position to buy the flat below the market price less than a week before being voted out of office last November.
The former president denies breaking any laws and says he took out an ordinary bank loan to buy the flat, located in a district off-limits to ordinary Romanians in communist times.
Though thrown out of office as head of state, Iliescu was elected a member of parliament in November and heads the opposition Party of Social Democracy.
